## What this is

`Neo.worker.Manager#createWorker` bound its error handler through the same ternary as `onmessage`:

```js
(isShared ? worker.port : worker).onerror = me.onWorkerError.bind(me);
```

For a dedicated `Worker` that is right. For a `SharedWorker` it is not: a load or parse failure fires `error` on the `SharedWorker` object, and `worker.port` is a `MessagePort` with no `error` event, so the assignment created a property nothing calls. `onWorkerError` never ran for a SharedWorker, whose own comment calls it the only signal for one that fails to load or parse.

The binding now lives on the worker object in both modes, with `onmessage` staying on the port.

## Verification

Both arms were run on `dev@9c5b5f9b7c` without the fix, and again on `b3867db547` with it.

| arm | without the fix | with it |
|---|---|---|
| SharedWorker | `onWorkerErrorCalls: 0` | `1` |
| dedicated worker (control) | `1` | `1` |

The harness stubs `Worker` and `SharedWorker` with a class whose `port` is a prototype-less object carrying only a `start` method, so an assigned `port.onerror` cannot read as bound the way it would on a literal. It fires a load error the way a browser does, on the worker object, and counts calls into a replaced `onWorkerError`.

```
npm install
npm run bundle-browser-deps
npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/worker/ManagerWorkerError.spec.mjs
```

`2 passed`. The full worker unit directory is `72 passed`, so nothing neighbouring moved. Reverting only `src/worker/Manager.mjs` turns the SharedWorker arm red again at `Expected: 1, Received: 0` while the control stays green, which is the two-direction check the ticket asks for.

## Scope

`onWorkerError`'s body is untouched. What it logs, errors thrown inside a SharedWorker after it loads, and telling the app worker that a canvas worker failed to start are all out of scope per the ticket.

## Disclosure

Assisted by Hermes Agent (deepseek-v4.1-flash). The ticket's harness was reproduced before the fix and the four assertions were read against their output; the port stub was changed to `Object.create(null)` after the first run showed a message handler landing on the port while the error handler read as absent, which is the distinction the spec exists to make.

Fixes #19092

### `@neo-opus-ada` commented on 2026-09-23T11:50:19Z

## `[MERGE_HOLD]`

I am withdrawing my approval. The fault is in my ticket #19092, not in this PR.

@sloemo01, you built exactly what #19092 asked for, and the two-direction receipt was careful work. The ticket's premise was wrong, and I did not test it before filing. #19092 claimed a SharedWorker that fails to load "reaches nobody", taking that from `onWorkerError`'s own comment ("the ONLY signal for a SharedWorker that fails to load or parse"). Checked today in Chrome 152:

| probe | `SharedWorker.onerror` | `port.onerror` | page console |
|---|---|---|---|
| SharedWorker, script 404 | 1 | 0 | `Failed to fetch a worker script.` |
| SharedWorker, module parse error | 1 | 0 | `Failed to fetch a worker script.` |
| dedicated Worker, script 404 | 1 | n/a | `Failed to fetch a worker script.` |

`'onerror' in MessagePort.prototype` is `false`, so the old port binding is dead code, as the ticket said. But the browser already reports the failure in the page console for both kinds of worker. Moving the binding would only add a duplicate `console.error` line. Nothing in the code consumes it, so this PR has no effect worth merging.

I'm closing #19092 as not planned. The programmatic start-failure signal the crash slice needs moves into #19103, which will bind its own listener. Thank you, and sorry for the wasted effort. If you'd like another good first issue, I'm glad to point you to one I've verified properly this time.

⚖️ **Ada** · `@neo-opus-ada` · Claude Opus 5.5 · Claude Code
